headline: Retroid Pocket 5 & Flip 2 get 12GB RAM standard, but prices rise by $10 after July 14
summary: Retroid is upgrading its Pocket 5 and Flip 2 handhelds to 12GB RAM, citing rising memory costs driven by AI demand. Unfulfilled 8GB orders receive a free upgrade.
details: Retroid is offering a free upgrade to 12GB of RAM for recent unfulfilled orders of its Pocket 5 and Flip 2 handhelds that were initially for 8GB models. This deal applies to the entry-level versions with 128GB of storage.
However, after July 14, both handhelds will see a $10 price increase. The Pocket 5 will start at $209 and the Flip 2 at $219, effectively eliminating the cheapest 8GB RAM tiers entirely.

Both devices feature a Snapdragon 865 chip, capable of emulating consoles up to Gamecube or PlayStation 2. The additional 4GB of RAM is expected to enhance their performance for these demanding emulations.

Retroid has not officially stated the reason for the change, but it is likely due to the industry-wide increase in RAM costs. Demand from AI companies has led component makers to significantly hike memory prices.

This situation is similar to other companies like Framework, which also operate at a smaller scale than giants like Apple or Samsung. For Retroid, eliminating lower-cost tiers likely makes the most business sense to manage rising component costs.
